questions.question: What will `console.log(typeof NaN)` output in modern JavaScript?
options: 'number'
'undefined'
'NaN'
'object'
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, NaN (Not-a-Number) is a special numeric value defined by IEEE 754, so its typeof is 'number'.

questions.question: Which keyword prevents reassignment of a variable binding while allowing internal mutation of object properties?
options: var
let
const
freeze
questions.explanation: `const` declares a block-scoped constant reference, meaning the identifier cannot be reassigned, but properties of an assigned object or array can still be modified.

questions.question: How does the JavaScript Event Loop handle microtasks (e.g. `Promise.then`) relative to macrotasks (e.g. `setTimeout`)?
options: Macrotasks are executed before microtasks always
All queued microtasks are drained immediately after each script or task execution before the next macrotask runs
Microtasks and macrotasks alternate execution one by one
They run in parallel on separate browser threads
questions.explanation: The microtask queue has strict priority over the macrotask queue. Once the current stack clears, the engine drains all microtasks before picking the next macrotask.

questions.question: What is the return value of `[1, 2, 3].reduce((acc, curr) => acc + curr, 10)`?
options: NaN
questions.explanation: The accumulator starts with initial value 10, then adds 1, 2, and 3, yielding 10 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 16.

questions.question: In standard closures, what does an inner function retain access to?
options: Only variables declared inside itself
Only global variables
Its outer (enclosing) function's lexical scope even after that outer function has returned
Only variables passed as formal parameters
questions.explanation: A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding state (lexical environment).

questions.question: Why should you never call React Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions?
options: It causes JavaScript syntax compilation errors
React relies on the call order of hooks across render cycles to preserve state bindings correctly
Hooks consume too much memory when called conditionally
Browser engines do not support dynamic functions
questions.explanation: React relies on a predictable array index based on the call order of hooks during each component render cycle.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the virtual DOM in React?
options: Directly replace the browser DOM with a web assembly canvas
Maintain a lightweight in-memory representation to compute minimal actual DOM mutations via reconciliation
Store component state in persistent local storage
Bypass CSS styling and render faster
questions.explanation: The Virtual DOM computes diffs (reconciliation) and batches updates so only necessary changes are pushed to the slow browser DOM.

questions.question: When should you provide a cleanup function inside `useEffect`?
options: Whenever a component makes a GET request
To unsubscribe from event listeners, clear intervals, or cancel pending network subscriptions when the component unmounts or before re-running the effect
Only when the dependency array is empty
Cleanup functions are deprecated in React 18+
questions.explanation: Cleanup functions execute when the component unmounts or prior to re-running the effect when dependencies change.

questions.question: How does Node.js achieve high concurrency despite running on a single main execution thread?
options: By spinning up a new OS thread for every incoming HTTP socket connection
Via non-blocking event-driven I/O supported by the libuv thread pool and OS asynchronous primitives
By executing JavaScript in multi-threaded parallel byte-code blocks
It cannot handle concurrency without third-party plugins
questions.explanation: Node.js utilizes an event loop with non-blocking I/O, delegating blocking tasks (DNS, file I/O, crypto) to libuv's background thread pool.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code must an idempotent REST API return when a resource is successfully updated with `PUT`?
options: 200 OK or 204 No Content
201 Created
304 Not Modified
400 Bad Request
questions.explanation: PUT updates a resource idempotently; returning 200 with the updated entity or 204 with no body is standard REST practice.

projects.title: Mission 1: Modern Responsive Developer Portfolio
projects.objective: Engineer a high-performance, mobile-responsive portfolio site showcasing your projects, technical skills, and interactive contact modal.
instructions: Use modern semantic HTML5 (`<header>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<footer>`).
Implement responsive layout using CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid without frameworks.
Support responsive media queries for mobile (<640px), tablet (<1024px) and desktop.
Add smooth scrolling and accessible form labels.
Push your code to a public GitHub repository.

rubrics.description: Valid HTML5 semantics and ARIA tags.
Flawless mobile, tablet and desktop layout.
Consistent spacing, dark theme contrast.
Clean commit history and structured README.

projects.title: Mission 2: Interactive Dynamic Budget & Expense Engine
projects.objective: Build an interactive financial calculation dashboard with dynamic DOM manipulation, real-time balance totals, and local storage caching.
instructions: Create entry forms for income and expense transactions with validation.
Dynamically create and append DOM cards for each recorded transaction.
Recalculate total balance, cumulative income, and total expenses automatically using `reduce()`.
Persist transaction records across page refreshes via `localStorage`.
Implement categorical filtering (food, rent, tech, education).

rubrics.description: Clean event listeners and element generation.
Accurate mathematical reduction and edge cases.
LocalStorage and form input boundary checks.
Modular JS functions, descriptive variable names.

projects.title: Mission 3: React Flow - Agile Task & Kanban Manager
projects.objective: Develop a component-driven Kanban board with customizable columns, priority tags, search filters, and reactive state updates.
instructions: Decompose UI into modular React components (`Column`, `TaskCard`, `NewTaskModal`, `FilterBar`).
Manage task state using React `useState` and `useReducer` for complex actions.
Enable moving tasks between 'To Do', 'In Progress', and 'Completed' lanes.
Add search bar filtering tasks by title, tag, or priority.
Demonstrate custom hooks for state synchronization.

rubrics.description: Clean props passing, reusability, single responsibility.
Proper use of hooks and immutable state patterns.
Smooth column transitions and responsive layout.
Handling empty columns and validation errors.

projects.title: Mission 4: Resilient RESTful API with Authentication
projects.objective: Architect a robust backend REST API featuring JWT authentication, route protection middleware, schema validation, and database CRUD operations.
instructions: Setup Express application with structured controllers, routes, and middleware.
Implement `POST /auth/register` and `POST /auth/login` with password hashing (`bcrypt`) and JWT issuance.
Build authentication middleware verifying Bearer tokens on protected endpoints.
Implement CRUD endpoints for user resources with status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 500).
Connect routes to SQLite or MongoDB database with transactional safety.

rubrics.description: Strict HTTP semantics, idempotency, JSON schemas.
Safe password hashing, JWT expiry, token extraction.
Normalized relational schema or clean document design.
Global centralized error middleware and audit logs.

projects.title: Mission 5: Full-Stack Career Intelligence Engine
projects.objective: Assemble an end-to-end full-stack web application uniting a React interface with a Node.js REST API and persistent database.
instructions: Connect React client to backend Express server via asynchronous API fetch/axios.
Store authentication tokens securely in client state and attach to HTTP headers.
Render real-time data visualizations (charts, status badges) based on server data.
Implement optimistic UI updates with error rollback handling.
Deploy or bundle both frontend and backend for production execution.

rubrics.description: Seamless client-server protocol and state synchronization.
All promised features work without runtime breaks.
Clean async handling, modular imports, defensive coding.
Professional futuristic styling and feedback toasts.
